statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6475 (PostgreSQL pg_basebackup and pg_rewind can overwrite unrelated files of origin superuser choice) in 16.14 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6475/ lists 16.14 as the fixed release for major version 16 (versions before 16.14 are affected), and the 16.14 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.14/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/6778af13e283c593fe0c16aeb6ed953a080e582b on the REL_16_STABLE branch, which changes src/bin/pg_basebackup/bbstreamer_file.c, src/bin/pg_basebackup/bbstreamer_tar.c, src/bin/pg_rewind/file_ops.c and src/port/path.c so that pg_basebackup and pg_rewind refuse unsafe paths and link targets; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-6475 and is in the REL_16_14 release tag and not in REL_16_13. pg_rewind ships in the postgresql16 package and pg_basebackup in the postgresql16-client package. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 16.14-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/56de254843f841a99aedea4953a2dc9ec9338eb4/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, differs from the 16.13-r0 one only in the version and tarball checksum, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6475 under its 16.14-r0 secfixes. We checked /usr/libexec/postgresql16/pg_rewind and /usr/libexec/postgresql16/pg_basebackup (postgresql16 and postgresql16-client packages), with the server binary's version string for each build, in every postgresql16 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27, on both x86_64 and aarch64 (package checksums verified against the package index): 16.13-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.13 and is affected, while 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 report 16.14, 16.15 and 16.16 and carry the fix. As a check, pg_basebackup contains the error message this fix adds ('tar member has unsafe path name') and pg_rewind contains 'target file path is unsafe for open' in 16.14-r0, 16.15-r0 and 16.16-r0 on both architectures, and neither does in 16.13-r0. 16.14-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-6475 (PostgreSQL pg_basebackup and pg_rewind can overwrite unrelated files of origin superuser choice) in 17.10 on the PostgreSQL 17 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-6475/ lists 17.10 as the fixed release for major version 17 (versions before 17.10 are affected), and the 17.10 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.10/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/8f881e188bba9e9d8d63ca0b42cb2597ba828e03 on the REL_17_STABLE branch, which changes src/bin/pg_basebackup/bbstreamer_file.c, src/bin/pg_basebackup/bbstreamer_tar.c, src/bin/pg_rewind/file_ops.c, src/include/port.h and src/port/path.c so that pg_basebackup and pg_rewind refuse unsafe paths and link targets; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-6475 and is in the REL_17_10 release tag and not in REL_17_9. pg_rewind ships in the postgresql17 package and pg_basebackup in the postgresql17-client package. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; the 17.10-r0 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/2949d6752d74a3fb36bd772b9f993331fa6917e2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD, differs from the 17.9-r0 one only in the version, the tarball checksum and the secfixes list, applies no patch that touches the files this fix changes, and lists CVE-2026-6475 under its 17.10-r0 secfixes. We checked /usr/libexec/postgresql17/pg_rewind and /usr/libexec/postgresql17/pg_basebackup (postgresql17 and postgresql17-client packages), with the server binary's version string for each build, in every postgresql17 build published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI package repository as of 2026-11-27 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, with package checksums verified against the package index: 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 and 17.9-r0 report PostgreSQL 17.7, 17.8 and 17.9 and are affected, while 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 report 17.10, 17.11 and 17.12 and carry the fix. As a check, pg_basebackup contains the error messages this fix adds ('tar member has unsafe path name' and 'link target has unsafe path name') and pg_rewind contains 'target file path is unsafe for open' in 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0 on both architectures, and neither does in 17.7-r0, 17.8-r0 or 17.9-r0. 17.10-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix.
